chunks: Zurarah narrated from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام that he said:

There are four prayers that a man may perform at any hour: a prayer that you missed, so whenever you remember it, you perform it; the prayer of the two rak‘ahs of the obligatory tawaf; the eclipse prayer; and the prayer over the deceased. These, a man performs at all hours.

key_terms.السَّاعَاتِ: hours/times; indicating general permissibility across all times
key_terms.الْكُسُوفِ: eclipse; the special prayer performed for an eclipse
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person; referring to the funeral prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ: two rak‘ahs; the two prayer units connected to tawaf
key_terms.صَلَوَاتٍ: prayers; the acts of worship being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.طَوَافِ: circumambulation; here, the obligatory tawaf connected to hajj or ‘umrah rites
key_terms.فَاتَتْكَ: that you missed; referring to an omitted prayer requiring qaḍāʾ

ai.seo_question: Which prayers may be performed at any time of the day in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that four types of prayers are not restricted by ordinary disliked times and may be performed whenever their cause or remembrance occurs. It highlights the legal flexibility given for making up missed salat, performing the two rak‘ahs of obligatory tawaf, Salat al-Kusuf, and the prayer over the deceased.
